title: ACT X
subtitle: The Sand Market
rewardRelicDesc: You start each battle with +1 mana.

intro.title: THE SAND MARKET
intro.text:
The ley lines run straight through the desert, which the Sand Market has spent decades making commercially relevant. The market grew up around the ley convergence — vendors first, then traders, then mercenaries, then the Dune Baron, who saw the strategic value and started charging for it.

Everything here has a price. Including passage through it.

intro.title: THE DUNE BARON
intro.text:
The Dune Baron is not a warlord in any conventional sense. He's a businessman who happens to employ an army. The distinction matters to him. He'll explain it at length if you have the time.

You don't have the time. He knows this. He's going to make you spend it anyway.

He respects efficiency, but only if you can afford it.

intro.title: THE MARKET ROUTE
intro.text:
The ley lines converge beneath the market's central spire — the Dune Baron uses the energy surplus to power the lights, the forges, and the contract-binding seals that make his mercenary arrangements legally enforceable.

You need the convergence point. He isn't selling it.

You're going to take it. He'll probably factor this into his pricing for the next traveller.

outro.title: THE DUNE BARON SETTLES
outro.text:
The Dune Baron doesn't lose gracefully. He loses expensively — which means he calculates the cost of the outcome, determines it was within acceptable parameters, and files the result under 'resolved.'

The ley lines pulse through the market floor. The convergence point opens.

He's already thinking about what to charge the next person who shows up.

outro.title: WHAT HE SAID
outro.text:
'You fought well,' the Baron said. 'I'll give you that at no charge.'

You asked about the Golden Compass.

'Consider it a finder's fee,' he said. 'For finding the limits of my hospitality.'

outro.title: THE GOLDEN COMPASS
outro.text:
The Golden Compass sits warm in your palm — the Baron's personal navigation tool, used to track ley line convergences across the desert. It still points to them.

It also, apparently, makes you faster off the mark. The Baron claims he hadn't noticed that. You don't believe him.

The ley lines point on. The market recedes. The desert is, for once, quiet.

dune-approach.label: Dune Approach
dune-approach.description: The outer ring of the market. Raiders patrol the approach roads.

sand-shrine.label: Oasis Shrine
sand-shrine.description: A spring shrine at a desert oasis. The water is real. The hospitality is negotiable.

eventConfig.title: The Oasis Shrine
eventConfig.description: A small spring, clear and cold, ringed with worn offering-stones. Desert travellers have been leaving things here for centuries. Some of the things left behind are still there.

pools.label: Drink from the spring
pools.consequence: Something in it stings — lose 6 HP

pools.label: Drink from the spring
pools.consequence: A rare card among the offerings

pools.label: Search the offering-stones
pools.consequence: Something useful left behind — uncommon card

pools.label: Search the offering-stones
pools.consequence: The spring goes dry when you touch it. Eerie.

pools.label: Fill your reserves
pools.consequence: The water heals on the road — healed 8 HP

pools.label: Fill your reserves
pools.consequence: +18 crystals in trade goods from the cache

pools.label: Fill your reserves

dune-hollow.label: Dune Hollow
dune-hollow.description: A sheltered hollow in the dune line. Out of the wind and out of sight.

outer-bazaar.label: Outer Bazaar
outer-bazaar.description: The market's fringe traders. Lower prices than inside. Fewer questions.

market-crossing.label: Market Crossing
market-crossing.description: The contested main road into the market interior. The Baron's guard controls access.

sand-battery.label: Sand Battery
sand-battery.description: Desert artillery platforms. The Baron invested heavily in these.

mirage-vent.label: Mirage Cache
mirage-vent.description: A hidden supply depot the Baron's forces use. Not all of it is decoy.

eventConfig.title: The Mirage Cache
eventConfig.description: A concealed depot in the dune face — the Baron's forces maintain several, and not all of them are decoys. This one is real. The lock is good but not insurmountable.

pools.label: Open the cache
pools.consequence: It was a decoy — lose 12 HP

pools.label: Sell the contents
pools.consequence: One item worth keeping — uncommon card

pools.label: Sell the contents
pools.consequence: It was already empty. Someone beat you to it.

caravan-elite.label: Caravan Guard
caravan-elite.description: The Baron's contracted heavy escort. Expensive, effective, professional.

baron-approach.label: Baron's Gate
baron-approach.description: The inner market. The Dune Baron's personal forces take over from the hired guards.

trade-archive.label: Baron's Ledger
trade-archive.description: The Baron's records room. Every transaction since the market opened.

eventConfig.title: The Baron's Ledger
eventConfig.description: The Dune Baron's transaction records — every contract, every sale, every mercenary hired and dismissed since the market was established. His notes on the Fracture are in here. He logged it as a business disruption.

market-rest.label: Inner Quarters
market-rest.description: The Baron's personal guest quarters. Better than anything outside the market walls.

baron-vanguard.label: Baron's Retinue
baron-vanguard.description: The Dune Baron's personal guard. These ones aren't contractors.

dunebaron.label: The Dune Baron
dunebaron.description: Proprietor of the Sand Market. He treats this battle as a transaction.
bossDialogue: Everything has a price. Your passage through my market has one too. This is the negotiation.
I've hired the best. You're fighting the best. Consider it a compliment.
I don't lose deals. I renegotiate terms. You've forced a renegotiation.
